newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rally to crack 6000 barrier.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rally to crack 6000 barrier.

text.p: Toronto stocks rocketed further into the stratosphere on Thursday, as the market's key TSE 300 Index broke through 6000 points for the first time ever.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 32.24 points to close at 6018.25 in turnover of 68.3 million shares worth C$1.06 billion ($790 million).
The index also set an intraday high of 6018.70.
The index has soared more than 1100 points since July 29 with no significant reversals.
"It's very positive. The technicians like to see these milestones broken and it means onward and upward," said HSBC James Capel Canada market strategist Bob Boaz.
The TSE's rally was led by strong gains in financial services, consumer products, gold and utilities. The market's only significant losses were in transportation.
Advancing stocks easily outpaced declines 513 to 382 with 317 issues unchanged.
"What's going to be interesting is over the next few days whether it stays at this level. If it retraces its steps, it could be a while before it goes over 6000 again," he added.
But Boaz said even a small uptick in gold prices could help underpin the market's recent gains.

* Barrick Gold Corp. jumped 1.55 to close at 41.20 on 2.6 million shares, extending this week's heavy action after the Indonesian government told Bre-X Minerals Ltd. to negotiate with Barrick to carve up Bre-X's stake in the Busang gold deposit.
Bre-X ended flat at 21 on 1.9 million shares.
* Bank stocks were heavy traders as the group reports its year-end results. Toronto-Dominion Bank gained 0.15 to 37 on 1.0 million shares after posting a record annual profit on Thursday.
* Bank of Montreal gained 0.45 to 44.45 on 1.2 million shares. Scotiabank rose 0.80 to 46.85 on 1.1 million shares.

* Canadian Airlines rose 0.15 to 2.30 as investors betted that the troubled airline will hammer out an agreement with two employee unions that have so far refused to back a survival plan. Four other unions have agreed to support the airline's restructuring effort.
